shared-needs.text: Declared, not linked: the shared author writes these volumes and anchors; check.sh matches each need against shared/ when it lands. Nothing below points at a file that does not exist in this pull request.
shared-needs.need: 100 exists or in progress: seat.bundle, workspace, seat.heartbeat, pr.opened, ticket-set.draft; acts: the next node on the edge
200 done: seat.result outcome done with validated structured output; acts: the phase post step

412 precondition refused: seat.bundle.refused, workspace.refused (claim_overlap, aggregate, ticket_in_flight, head_moved), seat.result preflight (bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, lease_expired); acts: N-11, or N-03 for claim_overlap without an attempt
423 blocked: seat.result outcome blocked with a terminal_reason from the reason table; acts: N-11 by reason
500 failed after 3 or a defect: seat.bundle.failed, workspace.failed, phase.failed, validator.failed, launcher.defect; acts: N-11, or N-06 health then N-28 for a defect
a seat is one bounded process between a bundle plus workspace and a seat.result; no pane, no prompt, no nudge, no idle state

the exact claude -p flag set of N-15 section command (settings, --setting-sources local, --strict-mcp-config, dontAsk, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd, --output-format json, --json-schema, --session-id or --resume); no --fallback-model, no bypassPermissions on the host
seat.result is parsed by the launcher from the claude -p JSON envelope; a seat never posts its own record; a model's claim is data to verify
host seats use the owner's subscription login (setup-token once, user-initiated); pod seats get ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the launcher's pod spec; no seat ever reads or copies a token
heartbeats: latest per run_id (upsert with monotonic seq): lease token and generation, pid, progress_at, transcript_bytes, adopted (true after a launcher restart re-entered the beat loop)
leases: holder, fencing token, generation, expires_at; renew accepted only for the current generation (N-02)
every wait has a timeout and a fallback; no agent is a gate; nothing starts by typing; the system drives (dag.md section 7 rule 2 until the shared volume lands)

section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-15 runs one seat as one bounded process and always ends it in a seat.result record, written by the launcher from the harness's own result, never by the model. A seat exists only between its input (a bundle plus a workspace) and its output (seat.result): the owner's rule is then true by construction (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#4-d02-seat-contract, why).

It removes the three mechanisms that existed only because a seat was an interactive pane: the typed brief, the ACK nudge and the trust writer (rebuild/investigation/S04-agent-frameworks-seat-contracts.md#9-what-to-kill item 1), and it ends the condition the idle alarm reported: a one-shot run cannot sit idle; a run with no progress is killed by the stall timer and retried (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#19-d17-the-one-minute-idle-rule option B).

Limits are fields of the launch, enforced by the harness and the launcher: turns, spend, wall clock and stall. A dead run, a crashed launcher or a missing result still yields a record, so nothing downstream waits on a seat that is not there.

section.title: Input records: seat.bundle plus workspace
section.text: Two records with the same run_id: seat.bundle 100 (../N-13/record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.bundle) and workspace 100 (../N-14/record.schema.json#/$defs/workspace). The launcher starts when both exist for a run_id that has no seat.result. From the bundle it takes the paths, hashes, model, limits, session id, lease and build_mode; from the workspace it takes the cwd, branch and mode. The dispatch's deadline_at is carried in the bundle's lease and in the dispatch record the launcher reads once for the deadline.

section.title: Output records: seat.result always, seat.heartbeat while it runs
section.text: seat.heartbeat, code 100, every lease.heartbeat_seconds (default 30, shared/state-store.xml#config-keys; seats.json carries no copy of it) while the process lives: run_id, lease token and generation, pid, started_at, progress_at (the mtime of the session transcript, which moves on every model turn and tool call), transcript_bytes, stderr_bytes, turns_so_far when the stream reports it. The store keeps the latest heartbeat per run_id (an upsert keyed by run_id with a monotonic seq, table heartbeats), and the stall timer (N-12) compares progress_at with stall_seconds. A heartbeat also renews the ticket lease at N-02 with the fencing token; a renewal refused (token stale, generation moved) is a signal to kill the run: another holder exists.

seat.result, exactly one per run_id, idempotency_key = run_id. Fields: run_id, ticket, role, phase, attempt, outcome (done or blocked), code (200 for done, 423 for blocked), terminal_reason (success, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution, error_max_structured_output_retries, killed_deadline, killed_stall, killed_lease_lost, killed_by_record, crashed, no_result, schema_invalid, bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, lease_expired, output_rejected, seat_blocked), exit_code, signal, cost_usd, turns, session_id, model, started_at, finished_at, duration_seconds, permission_denials (count and the first five), structured (the phase's validated structured output, present only on done), result_path, stderr_path, transcript_path.

A done result is then handed to the phase's post step (N-16 close-out, N-17 draft put, N-19 verdict put) inside the same launcher call; the phase record (pr.opened, ticket-set.draft, review.passed or review.changes) is written after seat.result, by code, and a post step that fails turns the outcome into blocked with the post step's reason (section result).
Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.heartbeat and seat.result.

section.title: Mechanism: the launcher in the Go service
section.text: Package scheduler/internal/launcher. Run(ctx, bundle, workspace) returns nothing to its caller but the record it wrote; every exit path of the function ends in a seat.result put, including panics (a deferred recover writes blocked crashed). One goroutine per run; the process is a child of the service with its own process group so a kill reaches every grandchild.
section.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant S as Store N-01 participant L as launcher.Run participant P as claude -p (child process group) participant R as $COQ_STATE/seats/runs/run_id S-->>L: seat.bundle and workspace for run_id, no seat.result L->>L: verify bundle_hash over the four files; mismatch is 412 bundle_mismatch L->>R: write started.json (pid pending, argv, env keys, deadline_at, stall_seconds, heartbeat_seconds, lease token and generation, session_id, transcript_path) L->>P: start with cwd = workspace.path, stdout to result.json, stderr to stderr.log L->>R: update started.json with pid, pgid and process start time Note over L,R: beat(run) below is one function; a launcher restart re-enters it from started.json (section retries) loop beat(run) every heartbeat_seconds until exit, or until deadline_at from started.json L->>S: seat.heartbeat (progress_at from the transcript mtime) and lease renew L->>L: deadline passed, stall, lease lost or kill record: SIGTERM to pgid, 30 s, SIGKILL end P-->>L: exit code and result.json L->>L: parse result, validate structured output against output.schema.json L->>S: seat.result (200 done or 423 blocked), idempotency_key = run_id L->>L: phase post step (N-16, N-17 or N-19) when done L->>S: phase record (pr.opened, ticket-set.draft, review.*) or a second seat.result is never written: the post failure is a phase.failed record and N-11 reads it
section.step: Preflight. Recompute sha256 of the bundle's four files and compare with the record's hashes; a mismatch is seat.result blocked 423 bundle_mismatch without starting a process (a hand edit of a bundle cannot launch). Check the workspace path exists and git -C path rev-parse HEAD equals workspace.base_sha; a mismatch is blocked workspace_mismatch. Check the lease has not expired; expired is blocked lease_expired, and N-11 decides.

Environment. A minimal environment is built from scratch, not inherited: PATH, HOME, LANG, TZ=UTC, COQ_RUN_ID, COQ_TICKET, COQ_ROLE, COQ_WORKTREE, COQ_STATE, COQ_CACHE, COQ_BUILD_MODE, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_NAME from seats.json git identity, and the credential variable of section permissions. CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CLAUDE_PID, AI_AGENT, HERDR_* and RAIL_SURFACE are never set, so a seat cannot find a herdr socket or a parent session (specs/SPEC-04-herdr-seat-lifecycle.xml#s-seat unset list, carried forward as an allow-list instead of a deny-list).

Start. The command of section command, with cwd = workspace.path, stdin closed, stdout to result.json, stderr to stderr.log, a new process group, and a context whose deadline is min(dispatch.deadline_at, now plus limits.wall_clock_seconds). Before the process starts, started.json is written with everything the beat loop needs and nothing it must look up: deadline_at (the absolute UTC instant just computed), stall_seconds and heartbeat_seconds of the role, the lease token and generation, session_id, the transcript path, argv and the environment key names; after the start it is updated with pid, pgid and the process start time from /proc/<pid>/stat. started.json is the whole input of beat(run), so a restarted launcher re-enters the loop from the file alone (section retries).

Beat loop, one function beat(run) for a fresh start and for an adopted run alike. Every heartbeat_seconds: read the transcript mtime at started.json transcript_path, write seat.heartbeat (with adopted true when the launcher is not the parent), renew the lease with the token and generation from started.json. Kill conditions, checked each beat in this order: deadline_at from started.json passed (killed_deadline); now minus progress_at greater than stall_seconds (killed_stall); lease renewal refused (killed_lease_lost); a kill record for this run_id from N-12 or N-42 (killed_by_record). Kill is SIGTERM to the pgid from started.json, 30 s, then SIGKILL to the pgid; the launcher never signals a pid, so an adopted run and a child are killed by the same call. Exit is detected by the child wait for a child, and by /proc/<pid> with the recorded start time disappearing for an adopted run, so the loop sees an exit within one heartbeat_seconds either way. The loop has no path that runs past deadline_at plus the 30 s grace: that is the bound of every run, fresh or adopted.

Exit. Wait for the process; read result.json; parse the claude -p JSON envelope (type result, subtype, is_error, total_cost_usd, num_turns, session_id, structured_output, permission_denials); validate structured_output against output.schema.json. Map to outcome and terminal_reason by section result. Write seat.result. Remove the process group if anything survives.

Post step. On done, call the phase's post function with the structured output: N-16 closeout (push, pull request, pr.opened), N-17 (ticket-set.draft put), N-19 (review record put after the head check). The post function writes its own record or a phase.failed 500 with reason; it never rewrites seat.result.

section.title: The exact launch command
section.text: Host seat on the owner's subscription (D03, slice one):

Pod seat on the API key (when seats move to pods under D22 and D03): the same with --bare added and the key in the pod's environment from the factory namespace's secret-free path (N-21 has no secret access; the key arrives as an env var set by the launcher's pod spec from the host, never from a cluster secret). --bare skips hooks, CLAUDE.md, auto memory and plugins; on the host the same effect comes from --setting-sources local plus the rendered settings (the checklist proves it).

Resume (a rework attempt of N-16 after review.changes): --resume "$SESSION_ID" replaces --session-id, with the new brief as the prompt; the verdict is in the brief, so no wake is typed and none can be lost (S04 section 8 item 8).
Why no --fallback-model: a fallback silently changes the model the role names; a 529 overload is a crashed run that N-11 retries on the same model (memory right-size-agent-models).

Why no --permission-mode bypassPermissions on the host: under bypass an allow rule restricts nothing (herdr/bin/testpane.sh header), so the fence of N-13 would be prose; dontAsk makes the allow list the fence and a miss a recorded denial, never a prompt.

section.title: Turning the process result into the record

row.reason: schema_invalid: the seat ended without the contract's output
killed_deadline, killed_stall, killed_lease_lost or killed_by_record, whichever the launcher issued

row.structured: valid but the post step refuses it
row.reason: output_rejected with the post step's detail (for example pr_not_found, head_moved, no_observations)

section.text: The structured output claims nothing on its own: N-16 checks the pull request exists at the claimed head, N-19 checks the head sha is the dispatched one, N-18 runs the acceptance commands. A model's claim is data to verify, never a verdict (rebuild/investigation/02-MAPPING.md#4-in-the-field-untouched-here-steal T04).

A seat that writes blocked itself: the output schema of every phase has an optional blocked object (reason, observations, repro); a valid output with blocked set is outcome blocked 423 reason seat_blocked with the observations attached; the seat never posts a record, the launcher does.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: The seat controller (N-06 unit, N-07 tick) lists run_ids that have both a seat.bundle and a workspace and no seat.result and no live launcher goroutine, and starts Run for each up to the capacity of seats.json max_runs (default from RAM: floor((host_ram_gib minus 8) divided by 1.5), the hosting guide's formula with 1.5 GiB per session, capped by workspace_slots). A run never starts from a pane, a prompt, a Makefile target typed by hand, or a person. After a service restart the same list recovers every run that was in flight (section retries).

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: min(dispatch.deadline_at, wall_clock_seconds of the role: worker 5400 s, spec-author 3600 s, reviewer 1200 s)
wait.fallback: SIGTERM, 30 s, SIGKILL; seat.result blocked killed_deadline; N-11 counts the attempt

wait.timeout: stall_seconds of the role: worker 600 s, spec-author 600 s, reviewer 300 s
wait.fallback: kill; blocked killed_stall (the stall timer N-12 reads the same heartbeat and can issue the kill record if the launcher's own check is late)
SIGKILL to the process group; survivors are listed in stderr.log and reported as a 500 defect

wait.what: an adopted process after a launcher restart (started.json without result.json, pid alive with the recorded start time)
wait.timeout: deadline_at from started.json, absolute, never recomputed; stall_seconds from started.json against the transcript mtime; the same beat(run) loop as a fresh start, so the bound is the remaining part of the run's own wall clock plus the 30 s grace
wait.attempts: 1 per run; every further restart adopts the same run against the same deadline_at, so the bound never grows
wait.fallback: SIGTERM to the pgid, 30 s, SIGKILL; seat.result blocked killed_deadline or killed_stall (or killed_lease_lost, killed_by_record) with adopted true and exit_code null; result.json present at that point is parsed as usual, absent is no_result; N-11 counts the attempt

wait.what: detecting the exit of an adopted process (a non-child cannot be waited on)
wait.timeout: one heartbeat_seconds: /proc/<pid> with the recorded start time is checked every beat
wait.fallback: the deadline wait above; a pid that is reused by another process is told apart by the start time, so a reuse reads as exited and result.json decides between the envelope's outcome and no_result
the beat is skipped and counted; three consecutive skipped beats kill the run with killed_lease_lost because liveness can no longer be proved to the store

the result stays in result.json beside a result.pending marker; the level-triggered recovery pass on the next tick re-puts it (idempotent by run_id) as its own step of 3; a marker older than one tick is reported by N-06 health as a store outage, and N-28 posts one card when it survives 3 ticks; the launcher itself never loops

wait.what: the API (529, 5xx, rate limit) inside the seat process
wait.timeout: the run's own bound, not the harness's: min(dispatch.deadline_at, wall_clock_seconds of the role) from the first wait, and stall_seconds when the retrying process stops writing its transcript
wait.attempts: 1 per run; the launcher never restarts the process and sets no retry flag of its own
wait.fallback: the run ends error_during_execution, killed_stall or killed_deadline, whichever comes first; N-11 backs off min(10 s times 2 to the n minus 1, 5 min) for 3 attempts, then dead and one card

section.text: No wait in this node depends on a person. The owner's only influence is a kill record from the Controls screen (N-42) which the heartbeat loop honours within one beat.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: Inside a run nothing is retried by the launcher: a run is one attempt. Across runs N-11 owns the count: a seat.result blocked is a failure record; attempt n+1 is a new dispatch, a new bundle and a fresh workspace (or the ticket's branch), and a new run; after attempt 3 the ticket is dead and N-28 posts one card. The launcher's own mechanical steps (puts, file writes) retry 3 times with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s.

Recovery after a launcher restart, the adopt path: for every runs/<run_id>/started.json without result.json, read pid, pgid and the process start time. If /proc/<pid> exists with the same start time, the launcher adopts the run by calling the same beat(run) of mechanism step 4 with started.json as its only input: it emits seat.heartbeat every heartbeat_seconds with adopted true (so N-12 sees the run again from the first beat after the restart), renews the lease with the recorded token and generation, and kills on the same four conditions with the same SIGTERM to pgid, 30 s, SIGKILL path. The bound is deadline_at from started.json, which is absolute and never recomputed, plus stall_seconds against the transcript mtime, so an adopted run can live no longer than it could have under its first launcher, and a second or third restart adopts the same run against the same instant. When the process exits (seen by /proc within one beat) result.json is parsed as usual; a non-child cannot be waited on, so exit_code is recorded as null and the envelope carries the outcome; a kill of an adopted run records the kill reason, and no_result when the envelope was never written. If the process is gone at restart, write seat.result blocked crashed at once. No run is ever left without a result and no adopted run is ever without a bound; that is the checklist's recovery proof.

Restart overlap on the adopt path: started.json is read, never recreated, by the adopter, and the O_EXCL creation of collision 1 (section many-agents) belongs to the fresh start only, so a fresh start and an adopt for one run_id cannot both proceed; the fresh start loses because the file exists, and the adopter is the only writer of heartbeats for that run_id after the restart.

Retryable reasons (N-11 retries without a card): crashed, killed_stall, killed_deadline, error_during_execution, no_result, killed_lease_lost. Reasons that count as the seat's own failure and retry with the verdict attached: schema_invalid, seat_blocked, output_rejected, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd. The reason is data on the record so N-11 branches on it by table, never by reading prose.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Up to max_runs seats run at once, each a separate process group with its own cwd, bundle, session id and run directory; nothing is shared but the store and the mirror, and neither is written by a seat. The host's ~/.claude.json is written by Claude Code itself for every session; the launcher never writes it (the ensure_trust rewrite without a lock is retired, L11 F15), and -p sessions show no trust dialog, so the file is read-only from this node's side.

Collision 1, two launchers for one run_id (restart overlap, or the adopt path racing a fresh start): started.json is created with O_EXCL; the second creator loses and exits; an adopter never creates it, only reads it, so a fresh start cannot win against a run that already has started.json (section retries, adopt); seat.result is idempotent by run_id and the store refuses a second put with 409, which the loser ignores. Two adopters of one run (the launcher's single-instance lock in state-paths makes this a defect, not a state) would both signal the same pgid and both put the same seat.result; the process dies once and the second put is the same 409.

Collision 2, two runs for one ticket (a lease fencing failure upstream): every heartbeat renews with the token and generation the bundle carries; the lease service accepts only the current generation, so the stale run's renewal is refused and it kills itself with killed_lease_lost within one beat. The winner is the one the lease names, never the one that started first.

Collision 3, the stall timer (N-12) and the launcher both decide to kill: both write a kill record idempotent by (run_id, reason); the process is killed once; the seat.result names the first reason recorded.
Collision 4, the owner's kill from the Controls screen while a kill is in progress: the same kill record path; the owner's reason wins on the record only if it is first.

Collision 5, two seats on the host share one subscription: a rate-limited seat is bounded by its own stall and wall clock (section waits), never by the harness's retry; it ends error_during_execution, killed_stall or killed_deadline and N-11 backs off. The capacity formula bounds concurrent seats so RAM, not the subscription, is the first limit; a subscription that runs out (the 53 hour rime stop, rebuild/investigation/L09-earlier-factory-iterations.md section 5.2) shows as a streak of error_during_execution with api_error_status 401 or 429 on the Alerts screen, and N-28 posts one card after 3 dead tickets in a row with that status.

Collision 6, transcripts: Claude Code keys transcripts by cwd and session id; every run has its own slot directory and its own UUID, so no two runs share a transcript path. The launcher copies the transcript into the run directory at exit so cleanup of ~/.claude/projects by Claude Code's own retention cannot lose the evidence.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: Alive with progress_at. Acts: N-12 reads; nobody else.
Outcome done with validated structured output. Acts: the phase post step in the same call.
Outcome blocked with a terminal_reason. Acts: N-11 by the reason table.
Preflight refused: bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, lease_expired. Acts: N-11; a bundle_mismatch is also a defect because something edited a bundle.
A post step (push, pull request, record put) failed 3 times after a done run. Acts: N-11; the run's work is on the branch, so attempt n+1 resumes from the branch, not from scratch.
A process survived SIGKILL, a result put never landed, or two launchers disagreed. Acts: N-06 health; N-28 after 3.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.writes: started.json (the beat loop's whole input: pid, pgid, process start time, deadline_at, stall_seconds, heartbeat_seconds, lease token and generation, session_id, transcript_path, argv, env key names), result.json, result.pending (only until the seat.result put commits), stderr.log, heartbeat.json (latest), transcript.jsonl (copied at exit), provision.log (N-14), closeout.log (N-16)
path.retention: 7 days after seat.result; 30 days for runs whose ticket died, so a card's evidence survives

section.path: Dry run by default; --apply deletes; never deletes a run directory without result.json younger than its deadline plus 1 hour; registered in N-45's scheduler/config/cleanup.json as seat-runs.

path.cleanup: Claude Code's own retention plus scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-runs.sh --transcripts
path.retention: the copy in the run directory is the evidence; the original may go at any time

section.path: The cleanup script removes transcripts of finished runs older than 7 days so the slot path's project directory does not grow without bound.

path.cleanup: released on exit; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-runs.sh --lock removes a stale lock whose pid is dead
path.retention: P0D when no launcher pid holds it

section.text: Nothing is written into a workspace by the launcher except what the seat itself writes inside its allow paths; nothing is written into the repository.

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The launcher (Go service, the owner's user on the WSL host): spawn processes, read the bundle, read and write the run directory, gRPC to the store, signal its own process groups. The subscription credential is the host user's Claude login (claude setup-token performed once by the owner by hand, the one user-initiated step, recorded as a runbook item); the launcher never reads or copies the token and never writes ~/.claude.json.

A pod seat: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the pod environment set by the launcher's pod spec (the host holds the key under $COQ_STATE/secrets/anthropic.key, mode 0600, outside the repository, with its own cleanup entry), --bare, bypassPermissions inside the pod because the pod is the fence (D23: no secret access, egress to GitHub and GHCR only).

A seat may never: read another run's directory (COQ_RUN_ID is the only one it knows and the directory is not in its allow paths), spawn a background process that outlives it (the process group kill ends it, and a survivor is a 500 defect), or reach herdr (no socket variable is set).

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/launcher -run TestAlwaysResult: fixtures for success, max turns, non-zero exit, SIGKILL, result.json missing, launcher panic; each yields exactly one seat.result with the mapped reason

section.item: Every exit path ends in a seat.result.

item.proof: go test TestStallKill with the fake clock: a process whose transcript mtime stops moving is SIGTERMed at stall_seconds and SIGKILLed 30 s later; the result reads killed_stall

section.item: The stall bound is enforced by the launcher.

item.proof: go test TestDeadlineKill with the fake clock: killed_deadline at the dispatch deadline even when progress continues
go test TestLeaseLost: a lease service that refuses the renewal makes the launcher kill the run within one beat; the result reads killed_lease_lost

go test TestRecoverAdopt and TestRecoverCrashed: started.json without result.json and a live pid is adopted into beat(run); the test asserts a seat.heartbeat with adopted true within one heartbeat_seconds of the restart, then the process exits and the result is parsed with exit_code null; a dead pid yields blocked crashed

section.item: Restart recovery leaves no run without a result and re-enters the beat loop.

item.proof: go test TestRecoverAdoptStall and TestRecoverAdoptDeadline with the fake clock: an adopted process whose transcript stops moving is SIGTERMed to its pgid at stall_seconds and SIGKILLed 30 s later with killed_stall; an adopted process with deadline_at in started.json already past is killed on the first beat with killed_deadline; a second adopt of the same started.json produces the same deadline_at

section.item: An adopted run has the same bound as a fresh one and the bound never grows across restarts.

item.proof: probe on the test host: a marker-writing user hook and a user MCP server are installed; a seat launched by the exact command writes no marker and reports no MCP server

section.item: The command loads no user layer on a subscription login.

item.proof: probe: a seat whose brief asks it to edit a file outside its allow paths ends with permission_denials naming the path and no change on disk

section.item: dontAsk plus the rendered fence refuses without a prompt.

item.proof: go test TestIdempotentResult: two Run calls for one run_id commit one seat.result; the second sees 409 and exits 0

section.item: One result per run under concurrency.

item.proof: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-runs.sh --dry-run lists finished runs older than 7 days and keeps a run with a dead ticket under 30 days; --apply removes the first set only

section.item: Cleanup exists and keeps card evidence.

item.proof: scheduler status (gRPC) lists every live run with run_id, ticket, role, pid, started_at, last progress_at, cost so far

section.item: Monitoring is the system reporting on itself.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: StatusResponse.seats (scheduler.proto SeatStatus, extended by its ticket with run_id, pid, progress_at, cost_usd, turns): one row per live run. Counters: runs_started, runs_done, runs_blocked_by_reason (a label per terminal_reason), runs_recovered_adopted, runs_recovered_crashed, heartbeats_skipped, cost_usd_total by role, turns_total by role. The Map screen (N-38) draws each live run as an inserter on the node's belt; the Machine screen (N-39) shows the run's progress_at age and cost; the Stats screen (N-40) binds to the counters; the Alerts screen (N-41) shows killed_stall, crashed and a 401 or 429 api_error_status streak.

Health line: live runs over capacity, the oldest progress_at age, the count of live adopted runs (each adopted run reports in the same seats row with adopted true, so the Machine screen shows it like any run), and the last seat.result at. A launcher with zero live runs while dispatches exist for longer than one tick is a health warning: capacity unused is a reconciler defect (D17).

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See a run: ls $COQ_STATE/seats/runs/<run_id>/; the brief is in the bundle (N-13); result.json is the harness envelope; stderr.log carries the launcher's own lines prefixed launcher:; transcript.jsonl is the evidence.

Resume a done run's session by hand for inspection: claude --resume <session_id> in the slot directory, as the owner, read-only intent; never on a live run (the lease is held) and never to continue the work: the follow-up is a new dispatch.

Restart the service while seats run: nothing to do by hand; the adopt path (section retries) re-enters the beat loop for every run with started.json and no result.json, and the first heartbeat after the restart carries adopted true; a run whose deadline_at passed during the outage is killed on the first beat with killed_deadline and N-11 retries it.

Kill a run: a control.action record from the Controls screen (N-42) with kind kill and run_id; the launcher honours it within one beat. Never kill -9 by hand; if it happens, the next tick records blocked crashed and the system continues.
Credential: claude setup-token once on the host as the owner (user-initiated); the launcher reports api_error_status 401 as an alert when it lapses; no agent runs the login.
Cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-runs.sh [--apply] [--older-than 7d] [--transcripts]; registered in N-45.

Break glass: the owner's one-time break glass (N-42) can start a dispatch outside the tick; the launcher still runs it through this node, with every limit, so there is no launch path that skips the result.
